name: Ahimelech
overview: Ahimelech was a male Levite known primarily as the son of Abiathar. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation with Levi and his familial connection to Abiathar, as recorded in 2 Samuel 8:17 and 1 Chronicles 24:6. There are no additional notes provided about his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahimelech means '[my] brother is king,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with significance related to kinship and authority. He is also referred to as Abimelech, which means '[my] father is king or [my] father is Molech,' indicating a variation in naming but not a divine bestowal of the name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ahimelech was the son of Abiathar, a relationship noted in 2 Samuel 8:17. Beyond this paternal connection, no other family relationships are documented in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Ahimelech's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his heritage as a Levite and his direct descent from Abiathar, who held a priestly role. This connection situates Ahimelech within the priestly lineage during the time of King David, underscoring the continuity of Levitical service in Israel's worship and governance as recorded in the Scriptures.
